commits.author: atqamar
commits.message:
(#10662)

Load each Megatron rank's remote checkpoint weights in merged byte-range requests instead of one request per tensor. On Snowball (5×8 H100, same frozen checkpoint, inputs and seed, expert-block sync), policy-worker startup falls from 209.9 s with [per-tensor reads](https://iris.oa.dev/#/job/%2Fatqamar%2Fusers-ahmad-checkpoints-startup-readiness-snowball-per_key-2026.11.06.6201-coordinator-28a2edc9) to 75.3 s with [prefetch](https://iris.oa.dev/#/job/%2Fatqamar%2Fusers-ahmad-checkpoints-startup-readiness-snowball-prefetch-2026.11.06.6202-coordinator-79ece35a).

`trainer.policy.model.remote_read_mode=prefetch` is the default for remote policy and reference weights; `per_key` reads one tensor per request. Prefetch reads only the tensors the rank owns, merges nearby byte ranges, and fetches windows of at most 1 GiB. A tensor larger than a window is fetched as a window of its own. A read that skips a planned tensor discards the buffered window and continues with range reads; closing the store logs a warning when any planned tensor was missed or left unused.

All 32 Snowball ranks read with no misses, no unused prefetched tensors and no individual reads. Each Qwen canary rank reads its checkpoint in 20 range requests with no misses. Tiny Hero loads tensors bitwise equal to its checkpoint with prefetch on [H100](https://iris.oa.dev/#/job/%2Fatqamar%2Fatqamar-startup-nov13-fixes-hero), and the nightly Grug Megatron lane runs that test.

commits.message:
[rl] Faster RL startup (1/2): Start ranks and workers without waiting (#10661)

Remove startup waits that do not depend on the model. On the Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct canary, training-job submission to the first evaluation falls from 391.0 s to 234.7 s (mean of two runs on 2×2 H100; main [1](https://iris.oa.dev/#/job/%2Fatqamar%2Fusers-ahmad-checkpoints-cat-count-canary-qwen2.5-0.5b-instruct-async-dry-b4e9ec7b-2026.11.06.6111-coordinator-1fc0f03b), [2](https://iris.oa.dev/#/job/%2Fatqamar%2Fusers-ahmad-checkpoints-cat-count-canary-qwen2.5-0.5b-instruct-async-dry-b4e9ec7b-2026.11.06.6115-coordinator-221bca17); this PR [1](https://iris.oa.dev/#/job/%2Fatqamar%2Fusers-ahmad-checkpoints-cat-count-canary-qwen2.5-0.5b-instruct-async-dry-b4e9ec7b-2026.11.06.6112-coordinator-587f8e3e), [2](https://iris.oa.dev/#/job/%2Fatqamar%2Fusers-ahmad-checkpoints-cat-count-canary-qwen2.5-0.5b-instruct-async-dry-b4e9ec7b-2026.11.06.6116-coordinator-78a87482)).

The driver creates every policy rank before it waits for rank 0's address, so rank constructors run concurrently. Rollout workers start together by default; a positive `start_interval_seconds` staggers them. If a worker fails to start, the started workers stay reachable for shutdown. The Megatron remote reader opens each shard once, without read-ahead, and closes it after loading. Datasets under 10,000 rows map and filter in the parent process. Bootstrap import checks run concurrently, readiness polls run every second, and the head rewrites its rendezvous file at most every five seconds.

The Qwen runs finish one training step with finite rewards and loss. A canary with a delayed second node shows rewrites about 5 s apart and both nodes joining. CPU tests cover the reader on Snowball's stacked and Hero's split expert layouts.

commits.author: atqamar
commits.message:
[rl] Start SkyRL attempt ids with a letter so YAML reads them as text (#11305)

Start every SkyRL attempt id with a letter, so the launcher records each
attempt under its own id.

Marin writes the launch document with PyYAML and the vendored launcher
reads it with OmegaConf. PyYAML leaves an id made of digits, one `e`,
and digits unquoted, and OmegaConf reads it as a float: `104e63883176`
becomes infinity, so the launcher names the attempt record `inf.json`
and returns `attempt_id: inf`, while Marin's run record carries the real
id. About 0.36% of ids drawn as twelve hex digits have that shape. An
attempt id is `a` followed by eleven hex digits, which both libraries
read as a string. Fingerprint builds use the literal `<attempt_id>`.

The launch-document census pins the id to those hex digits and fails
when the launcher loads `run.attempt_id` differently from how Marin
wrote it.

Reuse verified Hugging Face checkpoint exports on retry (#11210)

A retried object-store HF export request verifies an existing published
model and records the request complete without converting again.
Verification checks completion markers, manifest files, indexed shard
sizes, safetensors headers, and index agreement. A corrupt export is
reconverted; a conversion that exits without a complete export returns
the request to pending.

Requests that also publish to Hugging Face still run the exporter so a
failed Hub upload is retried. This makes object-store conversion safe to
retry after Iris reports a finalization failure even when the model was
already published.

commits.author: chrismc91
commits.message:
[shellbox] Add opt-in Daytona image builds for evals (#11410)

Daytona sandboxes can now build their image per sandbox instead of
starting from a named account snapshot. `DaytonaMachineFactory` and
Harbor's Daytona environment take `image_build`: `snapshot` (the
default, unchanged) or `declarative`, which passes the registry image or
Dockerfile straight to sandbox creation and creates no snapshot. Harbor
configs select it with `environment.kwargs.image_build: declarative`.

Snapshot mode needs one snapshot per distinct task environment.
SWE-bench Multilingual has 300 task images, and the eval account's
snapshot quota is 45. Declarative mode avoids the quota by rebuilding
the image for every trial, base-image pull included; repeat sandboxes
from one task image started in 2–6 s, which suggests Daytona caches the
builds. For the initial rollout, opt in only from evaluation policies
running in the Daytona eval account. RL training uses snapshots.
Enabling declarative builds in the RL account requires a separate change
from Daytona. `snapshot-specs` and `DaytonaMachineFactory.prepare()`
reject declarative configurations, since there is no snapshot to list or
prepare.

Marin keeps separate Daytona orgs for RL, data and evals, each with its
own key and build permissions, and declarative builds belong to the eval
org only. The eval launcher now reads only `DAYTONA_EVAL_API_KEY`
(launch environment, then the `hai-gcp-models` secret). Before, an
exported `DAYTONA_API_KEY` took precedence and could route evals into
another org. SkyRL's Harbor task settings reject `image_build`, and its
Harbor evaluation callback rejects `image_build: declarative` when the
trainer is configured. RL configs that point Daytona at the eval-org
key, such as `experiments/post_training/inventory/train_quick_loop.py`,
are left for a follow-up.

Before rebasing onto the snapshot refactor in #11202, this option ran
`swebench_multilingual@1.0` in the eval account: gold patches scored 299
of 300 (the remaining task fails its own gold patch), and 20-task
terminus-2 smoke runs for Qwen3.6-35B-A3B and Qwen3.5-35B-A3B had no
sandbox build or startup errors. After the rebase, a declarative sandbox
built from the `apache__druid-13704` task Dockerfile started in 36 s,
ran commands and was deleted on close. The SWE-bench Multilingual eval
configs that use this option follow in a separate PR.

commits.author: chrismc91
commits.message:
[evals] Add SimpleQA Verified as a curated evaluation (#11393)

### What

Adds two curated evaluations of [SimpleQA
Verified](https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.07968) (Google DeepMind). The
benchmark is 1,000 short questions, each with one factual answer, and
checks what a model knows without tools. An LLM judge grades each answer
as correct, incorrect, or not attempted. SimpleQA Verified is a cleaned
subset of OpenAI's
[SimpleQA](https://openai.com/index/introducing-simpleqa/), with
duplicates, ambiguous questions, and wrong gold answers removed or
fixed.

Data comes from
[`google/simpleqa-verified`](https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/simpleqa-verified)
at revision `0dc97e0d`. The judge prompt is Appendix A of the paper (CC
BY 4.0), the same text as the [Kaggle starter
notebook](https://www.kaggle.com/code/nanliao7/simpleqa-verified-benchmark-starter-code)
(v9). The judge is `openai/gpt-oss-120b` on Together; the leaderboard
uses `gpt-4.1`.

- `simpleqa-verified`: thinking off, 2,048-token cap.
- `simpleqa-verified-thinking`: thinking on, 16,384-token cap. This is
how the leaderboard models were compared.

Both keep each model's own sampling defaults, as the notebook does;
greedy decoding sent gpt-oss into repetition loops. The `final_only`
response selection from #11201 gives the judge only the model's final
answer, never its reasoning trace. Evaldash reports accuracy as the
primary metric, with F1 (the leaderboard's headline) beside it. Neither
evaluation is part of a suite.

### Why

#10234 asks for a working SimpleQA to score models on. Short-form
factual recall is expected to correlate with our out-of-distribution
AAII target, and the current SimpleQA implementation gives implausibly
low scores. SimpleQA Verified fixes the original's label noise. Its
not-attempted rate also shows how often a model abstains rather than
guesses wrong.

### Validation

Full 1,000-question runs on this branch, in percent:

| Model | Thinking | Accuracy | F1 | Not attempted | Truncated | Kaggle
F1 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| gemma-4-26B-A4B-it | on | 8.0 | 8.9 | 20.9 | 50 | 9.1 |
| gemma-4-26B-A4B-it | off | 6.5 | 6.9 | 10.7 | 2 | — |
| gpt-oss-20b | on | 6.2 | 6.3 | 2.5 | 0 | 5.9 |
| qwen3.6-35b-a3b | off | 17.9 | 18.0 | 0.6 | 14 | — |

With thinking on, both leaderboard models score within one standard
error of their leaderboard F1, despite the different judge. Every run
also agrees within one standard error with an earlier run through
vendored Evalchemy. A truncated response has an empty final answer and
is scored as not attempted.

A check over all 4,000 items confirmed four things:
- each model prompt is the bare question from the pinned dataset;
- each judge prompt is the template filled with the question, the gold
answer, and the final answer only;
- every judge reply is a single letter;
- the per-item metrics match the label.

An earlier blinded audit of 386 answers put the judge's error rate at
2.1% (95% CI 0.3–4.8%), leaning strict. In that audit, 99 of 100 gold
answers checked against web sources were confirmed and none were wrong.
Two blind reviewers (Opus and Sonnet) labelled all 194 answers on these
runs where the judge's label disagrees with a gold-text match. They
agreed on 187 (κ 0.93) and overruled the judge on 15, mostly answers
that name a wrong candidate and then correct themselves to the gold
answer, which the judge marks incorrect. Fixing those raises qwen3.6's
F1 by about 0.5 and moves the others by less.

One deliberate difference from the notebook: its parser grades a judge
reply of `NOT_ATTEMPTED` as correct. Marin accepts only a bare A, B, or
C and records anything else as a judge failure. The prompt comes from
the paper, which is CC BY 4.0, and the dataset is MIT-licensed.

### Cost

| Run | GPUs | Eval time | Start to finish | H100-hours |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| gpt-oss-20b, thinking on | 1 | 10 min | 15 min | 0.22 |
| qwen3.6-35b-a3b, thinking off | 4 | 10 min | 55 min | 3.5 |
| gemma-4-26B-A4B-it, off then on | 2 | 19 + 26 min | 58 min | 1.9 |

Eval times are slowed by #11391. The qwen3.6 server also sat idle for 43
minutes before its first request. Each run makes 1,000 judge calls,
about 1.8M input and 0.13M output tokens.

Depends on #11201; merge that first. The validation runs recorded this
selection under its earlier name, `final`, with identical behavior.

Replaces #11063, which targeted vendored Evalchemy before #10957 removed
it.

Part of #10234.

---------

Co-authored-by: loom <claude-max-1@openathena.ai>

commits.author: chrismc91
commits.message:
[taskcompendium] Add a final-only response selection (#11201)

Add `final_only` to `ResponseSelection`. It grades only the response's
final
content, never its reasoning, including when the content is empty or the
response hit the token limit. This matches Evalchemy's `final_only`
content
policy.

LLM judges need this option. The default, `combine`, prepends the
reasoning
trace to the answer. The `final_or_complete_*` options fall back to a
complete
trace when the content is empty. A judge reads the whole text, so in
both cases
it grades the candidate answers inside the trace. In a SimpleQA Verified
run
with gpt-oss-20b and thinking enabled, the judge received 5,212
characters of
reasoning followed by a one-line answer.

No benchmark uses the option yet. SimpleQA, SimpleQAMini and
FinanceBench keep
`combine`, the Evalchemy default.

commits.author: penfever
commits.message:
[shellbox] Extend Daytona output collection deadline (#11339)

Give Daytona a shared 60-second deadline to collect stdout and stderr
after a command exits. The deadline is configurable through
`DaytonaMachineFactory` and Harbor's Daytona environment. Command
execution and interrupt cleanup keep their existing timeouts.

In the 20-task Terminal-Bench 2.1 retest linked from #10735, six
single-task trials failed with `Cannot collect Daytona command output`.
Three expired while requesting a stream's byte count and three while
downloading a stream. All six had completed the command and then spent
the prior shared 10-second deadline awaiting Daytona HTTP response
headers. The successful trial archive contains 199 agent-visible
terminal responses (mean 2.2 KiB, maximum 10,201 bytes), but those
responses are display-capped. Twelve verifier stdout files averaged 23.5
KiB and reached 86.3 KiB. Raw per-command files are removed after
collection, so their historical sizes cannot be recovered from that
archive.

A CPU-only benchmark in the same CoreWeave RNO2A region used eight
concurrent Daytona sandboxes. Each held one `process.exec` request like
the terminal supervisor in the failed evaluation. At each raw file size,
it recorded 24 direct transfers and 24 paired collections (288
measurements total). Direct transfer fetched the whole file. Paired
collection followed Shellbox's count, optional clip, download, and
clipped-file removal for both streams; it fetched at most 1 MiB per
stream, Shellbox's default output limit. Command-directory cleanup
remains separately bounded. This load test measures deadline headroom;
it cannot identify the provider-side cause of the archived stalls. Times
are seconds; P95 uses the nearest-rank sample.

| Raw file size | Direct download mean / P95 | Paired collection mean /
P95 |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| 0 B | 0.54 / 1.01 | 2.53 / 3.76 |
| 16 KiB | 0.69 / 1.23 | 2.60 / 3.73 |
| 256 KiB | 0.67 / 1.19 | 2.41 / 3.50 |
| 1 MiB | 0.66 / 1.07 | 2.49 / 3.36 |
| 8 MiB | 0.82 / 1.36 | 5.83 / 7.37 |
| 32 MiB | 0.76 / 1.13 | 3.44 / 5.02 |

All 288 measurements completed. Without held requests, paired collection
at 8 MiB had a 1.10-second mean and 1.32-second P95. The held-request 8
MiB maximum was 7.64 seconds, close to the former 10-second deadline;
the nonmonotonic size results limit extrapolation from this short
sample. The 60-second limit gives that path headroom while remaining
bounded. A live `DaytonaMachine.run` smoke with 8 MiB on each stream and
a held request passed, and the Linux deadline regression test passed on
RNO2A. The broad Harbor suite passed 1,915 tests; three
terminal-cancellation tests failed on macOS with the same failure on
unmodified main.

Raw [held-request
measurements](https://filer.marina.oa.dev/#s3%3A%2F%2Fmarin-us-east-08a%2Fmarin%2Fbenchmarks%2Fshellbox%2Fdaytona-output-20261113%2Fload8-held.json)
(`s3://marin-us-east-08a/marin/benchmarks/shellbox/daytona-output-20261113/load8-held.json`),
[baseline
measurements](https://filer.marina.oa.dev/#s3%3A%2F%2Fmarin-us-east-08a%2Fmarin%2Fbenchmarks%2Fshellbox%2Fdaytona-output-20261113%2Fload8.json)
(`s3://marin-us-east-08a/marin/benchmarks/shellbox/daytona-output-20261113/load8.json`),
and the [benchmark
script](https://filer.marina.oa.dev/#s3%3A%2F%2Fmarin-us-east-08a%2Fmarin%2Fbenchmarks%2Fshellbox%2Fdaytona-output-20261113%2Fbenchmark_daytona_output.py)
(`s3://marin-us-east-08a/marin/benchmarks/shellbox/daytona-output-20261113/benchmark_daytona_output.py`)
are retained for reproduction.

with Torch 2.14.1/cu132, Megatron Core 0.18, Megatron Bridge 0.6 and
stock Transformer Engine (TE) 2.21. Use published FA3 3.0.1 for H100/x86
training and FA4 4.0.0b39 for GB200/ARM training, replacing custom FA2
wheels. Replace Speculators wheel rewriting with the paired
[Speculators/hs-connectors fork
release](https://github.com/marin-community/speculators/releases/tag/v0.8.0%2Bmarin.1).
Standalone serving and TPU adoption remain in #11241 and #11285.

Grug BF16 selects FlashAttention. Native TE remains the expert-matmul
default; Blackwell uses Torch for the first expert projection only with
`batch_invariant=true`. Parameter names and checkpoint layout stay
unchanged. Fix attention enum selection, let Core govern the GPU-test
attention environment and remove the obsolete FA2 startup import. Retain
Speculators verifier compatibility; the EAGLE vocabulary-map checkpoint
repair remains separate as P1 in #11377.

Numerical checks pass with unchanged tolerances on both GPUs; 457 CPU
checks pass. Full 535B Mochi qualification restored checkpoint 13,
completed four updates through 17, consumed updated weights and saved
checkpoint 17 with matching trainer/optimizer/scheduler counters. Two
updates had nonzero gradients; the other two batches had zero
advantages. Sequences reached 65,360 tokens. The run used 48 training
and 12 inference GPUs on [preserved source
c2081d90](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/c2081d90bf8b79005a8b3d60320b51128658131f).
Newer loop, MuonH and publication refactors have only small-scale
coverage.

The Mochi test recipe disables CUDA graphs for DP12/EP12
`allgather_reducescatter`, retaining compilation mode 3. This PR leaves
serving graph defaults unchanged. The earlier graph-enabled run failed
after weight publication; its cause is unknown and the full-model
performance cost is unmeasured. TE's PyTorch binding still uses a source
build, and existing dependency exceptions remain below.

<details>
<summary>Wheel builds and retained dependency exceptions</summary>

TE's GPU library uses NVIDIA wheels. Its PyTorch binding is [built from
unchanged
source](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/releases/tag/skyrl-native-te221-cu132torch2141-20261113-0821e3af):
no CUDA 13 ARM wheel is published; the official CUDA 13 x86 binding
targets NVIDIA container 26.08 and has not been qualified with our
stack. [Upstream
#3310](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TransformerEngine/issues/3310) and
[#3311](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TransformerEngine/pull/3311) address
CUDA 13 wheel coverage; #3311 targets Torch 2.11. Core and Bridge need
no internal patches.

CPU Torch stays at 2.11 to preserve the existing CPU profile; the GPU
upgrade does not require changing it.

Retained exceptions: causal-conv1d/Mamba patches, Bridge's
Transformers/FlashInfer overrides and omitted NVRx restart/Hadamard
quantization dependencies, OpenTelemetry 1.44, Rigging below declared
version floors and the ARM cuSPARSELt tag workaround. Other Bridge
adapters and learning quality remain unqualified.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Numerical diagnostics and attention timings</summary>

The tested cuDNN path changed Grug BF16 train/eval log-probabilities by
0.163 against a 0.001 limit; FlashAttention passes. Changing peer
batches moved native TE log-probabilities by 0.44; the Torch expert
projection kept them unchanged. Gradient and post-update trainer/serving
checks pass at existing tolerances.

| Matched attention forward/backward | FA2 | Selected package |
| --- | --- | --- |
| H100: one packed 16K sequence and one 32K sequence | 73.50 ms | 40.64
ms (FA3) |
| H100: same batch, 2,048-token window | 15.18 ms | 9.63 ms (FA3) |
| GB200: near 65K, CP4 | 115.53 ms | 38.55 ms (FA4) |
| GB200: windowed | 12.90 ms | 7.12 ms (FA4) |

The earlier H100 batch with 1,024/1,536-token sequences was 11% slower.
These attention timings do not measure full-model throughput.

</details>

<details>
<summary>CUDA-graph failure and measured fallback cost</summary>

Graph replay failed after weight publication to inference workers.
[Upstream #59646](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/59646)
proposes disabling graphs for the same backend. Small cases passed both
graph settings, so the cause remains unisolated. A tiny serving test
took 4.47 seconds without graphs versus 1.87 with them; full-model cost
is unmeasured.

</details>
